title: Constant pulsations produce large eclipse statistics with coarse phase bins in a KIC 3230227 sampling test
abstract: We test eclipse changes of three known non-orbital pulsations in Kepler release 25 data for KIC 3230227. With 300 constant phase bins, joint six-coefficient statistics are 57.69 for aperture flux and 63.03 for corrected flux. With 700 bins, they are 0.72 and 4.59. A constructed light curve with constant pulsations and a resolved binary template gives statistics of 62.71 and 62.55 at the same coarse resolution and observed times. These tests show that a coarse eclipse model can give false evidence for mode changes in this sampling test. Finer fits do not give a stable eclipse response. Errors remain large relative to mode amplitudes. The test does not locate the pulsating star, find a new mode, or give independent-instrument confirmation.

display.caption: Observed and constructed-data tests show strong dependence on phase resolution. The constructed light curve has constant mode amplitudes. Statistics are conditional diagnostics, not calibrated false-alarm probabilities.

citations.reason: Provides prior target context and the eclipse phase used for this different test.
